subject: E-sign & CLM renewals: decision timeline and consolidation options
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor renewals: Ironclad + e-sign options (need path by 3/16)

Team —

Heads-up: Ironclad contract for CLM and our e-sign integration both expire 2026-05-01. Procurement got the renewal quote yesterday (attached) and there are two upstream asks from Finance and Legal:

- Finance: can we reduce unit cost by consolidating DocuSign + CLM spend vs renewing Ironclad enterprise bundle?
- Legal: wants confirmation of preservation/audit-log exports and whether existing retention settings satisfy upcoming customer audit cycles.

Options on the table: renew Ironclad as-is; renegotiate Ironclad to remove e-sign and rely on DocuSign (separate vendor); or move CLM workflows to an alternative and standardize on DocuSign for signed artifacts.

Can each of you confirm by EOD Thu (3/12) whether Legal needs any change to SOW/terms and whether Procurement should push for a 12 or 24 month term? Finance would prefer 24 months if unit pricing improves.

Attachments: Ironclad_Renewal_Quote_2026.pdf, CLM-vs-ESign-Risk-Matrix.docx

Thanks —
Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor renewals: Ironclad + e-sign options (need path by 3/16)

Dev / Mark —

Quick legal read: the two items we care about for the contract are retention/export guarantees and subcontractor flow-down for any hosted signing provider. The Ironclad quote references standard SOC2 language but does not include the newer 3rd-party export SLA we requested last year. If Procurement can push for explicit export window (30 days TTL for raw exports) and a clause allowing audit log retention to be certified to our internal standard, Legal can sign off on either 12 or 24 months.

If we consider a split (Ironclad for CLM + DocuSign for e-sign), we need clear responsibility mapping for audit trails — who stores canonical signed PDFs and who owns the chain-of-custody metadata. That mapping must be in the SOW.

I added notes in CLM-vs-ESign-Risk-Matrix.docx.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor renewals: Ironclad + e-sign options (need path by 3/16)

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A few priorities from product/ops and finance perspective:

1) Continuity: minimal risk window. If the work to move signed artifacts is more than a 30-day project, we should prefer a one-year extension to avoid churn during H2 product launch cycles.
2) Cost: if a 24-month term buys us ~20% off the line items and reduces per-sign fees materially, I’m inclined to accept that for predictable unit economics.
3) Integration debt: Laura, please flag any SOW language that would increase implementation hours beyond what's in the renewal. Procurement, please ask Ironclad for an itemized breakdown of professional services vs. recurring fees.

I’m okay with Procurement opening a parallel conversation with DocuSign for comparison, but don’t let that slow the Ironclad negotiation. We should be able to accept a conditional 12-month with a 30-day exit if they can't hit export SLA.

-MK
Markus Klein
VP, Revenue Operations
markus_klein@redwood.ai

From: Kevin Ortiz <kevin.ortiz@docusign.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement Services <vendor@acme-procure.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: DocuSign consolidation estimate + audit-log capabilities

Hi Dev / Markus / Laura —

Thanks for the context. Based on your usage figures (approx 25k signatures/year) I attached a preliminary consolidation workbook (DocuSign_Consolidation_Costs.xlsx). Two notes:

- DocuSign can act as the canonical signing provider and store signed PDFs with chain-of-custody metadata. We can provide export APIs for signed artifacts and logs; those exports are retained for 90 days by default but we offer extended retention as an add-on.
- If you want DocuSign to replace Ironclad for CLM workflows, there will be a material implementation lift — DocuSign CLM (Agreement Cloud) is modular but not drop-in for our current Ironclad contracts. We estimate a 10-12 week migration with professional services.

If helpful, we can set up a 30-minute technical call next week with our integrations architect and your Legal Ops folks to walk through the export schema and retention SLAs.

Regards,
Kevin Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive, DocuSign
kevin.ortiz@docusign.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor renewals: decision timeline and consolidation options — recommendation

Team —

After reviewing the Ironclad quote and DocuSign workbook and speaking to Finance: recommendation to negotiate the following path by 3/23 and lock a short extension if Ironclad pushback threatens continuity:

1) Ask Ironclad for a 12-month renewal with: explicit 30-day export SLA, itemized PS vs recurring fees, and a 20% discount on the e-sign line item. If they accept, proceed with 12-month and revisit architecture for H1 2027.
2) In parallel, open a targeted DocuSign pilot for high-volume signing flows (sales/partner agreements) to validate migration effort and finalize cost comparison. Ask DocuSign for a technically scoped 4-week pilot (reduced PS hours).
3) Require Legal to sign the export and chain-of-custody clause as a condition of renewal approval (Laura, assigning to you).

I’ll place the Ironclad quote into the procurement queue and request redlines. If Ironclad refuses the export clause, we will take the 30-day extension and accelerate the DocuSign pilot.

Action items:
- Dev: submit RFQ follow-up to Ironclad (by 3/16) — DONE (ticket #IR-2026-77)
- Laura: prepare export clause template (by 3/18)
- Markus: confirm budget appetite for a short DocuSign pilot (reply by 3/17)

Thanks —
Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference
